sources.entry: jinja - A modern and designer-friendly templating language.

summary.one_liner: Jinja is a fast, expressive, extensible Python templating engine that renders documents from templates populated with data.
summary.what_it_does: Jinja lets template authors write Python-like placeholder syntax that is filled with data to produce final documents. The README lists template inheritance and inclusion, macros defined and imported within templates, and autoescaping for HTML to help prevent XSS from untrusted input. A sandboxed environment can render untrusted templates safely. It also offers AsyncIO support, I18N via Babel, and templates compiled to optimized Python code just-in-time (cached) or ahead-of-time. Filters, tests, functions, and syntax can be extended.
use_cases: Generating HTML pages from Python web app templates
Rendering reports or documents from data
Sharing reusable page layouts with block inheritance
Precompiling templates for faster production rendering
notable: Sandboxed environment for rendering untrusted templates
Template inheritance with blocks and macros
Autoescaping for HTML to mitigate XSS
Templates compiled to Python code, cached or ahead-of-time
Extensible filters, tests, functions, and syntax
caveats: README does not include installation or run instructions
README does not state a license
